author: Dcaseyb
title: DO NOT BUY!
body:
As a user for several years and constantly having to run down 3 flights of stairs to MANUALLY get my water heater to respond to this TERRIBLE system. I finally  just gave up and set up my own smart system to do what this thing was sold as being able to do.  Never had an issue since. The CEO of Rheem should be embarrassed !Buy a Bosch!  

Here is my technical assessment:

EcoNet Wi-Fi components specifically are where a lot of the issues originate. The actual water heater tanks and heat pump hardware are usually much better than the networking layer attached to them.

The pattern that shows up repeatedly is:

* the heater itself works,
* but the Wi-Fi/app ecosystem becomes unstable.

A lot of owners describe the system as:

* fragile,
* outdated,
* very picky about networks,
* and heavily dependent on Rheem’s cloud services.

Some recurring issues people report:

* “Wi -Fi connection error”
* random disconnects
* inability to reconnect after router changes
* getting stuck in Vacation mode
* schedules not saving
* app saying connected when it isn’t
* system disappearing from the app entirely
* reconnect loops after power outages

Those reports are extremely common across water-heater owners.  

One of the biggest technical problems is that these components are based on older 2.4 GHz IoT networking assumptions and often struggle with modern Wi-Fi environments:

* mesh networks,
* WPA3,
* combined SSIDs,
* client steering,
* modern roaming features,
* VLAN isolation,
* advanced firewalls.

People with:

* Eero,
* AT&T Internet Air,
* UniFi,
* modern ASUS systems,
* pfSense,
* enterprise APs,
    tend to hit problems disproportionately often.  

A very common workaround is:

* temporarily disabling 5 GHz,
* forcing WPA2 only,
* disabling WPA3,
* turning off cellular during pairing,
* using a separate legacy 2.4 GHz SSID.

That alone tells you the module stack is fairly dated.  

There are also reports suggesting the Wi-Fi component  themselves physically fail at a nontrivial rate:

* partial Bluetooth operation but dead Wi-Fi,
* corrupted firmware,
* failure after outages,
* intermittent control board communication.  

The architecture is also more cloud-dependent than many people realize. If Rheem’s backend has issues (and it seems to often):

* remote control may stop,
* schedules may fail,
* the app can show stale data,
* and in some cases units appear to retain the last cloud-issued state.  

That last point especially frustrates technically inclined users because:

* there is very limited local-first control,
* limited documentation,
* and limited transparency around APIs/protocols.

A lot of advanced users eventually bypass EcoNet entirely and use:

* Home Assistant integrations,
* ESPHome serial adapters,
* or direct diagnostic-port access.

There’s a pretty active DIY community around “making Rheem Wi-Fi products usable without EcoNet.”

From a systems-engineering perspective, the system feels like:

* low-cost IoT hardware,
* designed around minimal BOM cost,
* with a cloud-first software model,
* and relatively limited long-term software robustness.

The water heater itself is usually the stronger part of the product. The smart component often feels like an afterthought bolted onto an appliance platform rather than something architected as a robust control system.

author: otherguy
title: Don’t buy Rheem if you value good apps
body:
I’m not sure who the product manager in charge of this app is, but the Rheem furnace and heat pump sales team should banging on their door, asking them to fix it. This app is going to cost sales. I bet it already is. If I could return my heat pump system just on the back of this app experience, I would. As it is I’m recommending that the people I know that are installing new systems use anybody but Rheem if they value home automation or anything above minimally functional apps. 

Just getting rid of the stupid intro animation, or at least preloading the API calls while it runs would display something other than utter disdain for the users. Have the people that tested this app ever used an iPhone or did leadership just ignore every single piece of non-critical UX feedback that was logged?

Absolutely, the thing I want when I want to change the temperature in my house is an enforced 15 second delay from loading the app from a cold start. Every. Single. Time. 🤮

There’s no HomeKit support, no Matter, no multi-user geofencing for home/away. Home automation foundation Apple has already done for you: not available in this steaming pile of cross platform junk. 

Did I mention there’s apparently no local caching of data or background API calls, so every tap is like loading the slowest website you’ve ever used?

I bet you I could vibe code a native swift UI app with better experience on top of the existing clearblade API with a clever prompt, a $200 max plan, and a week or two. I bet you could have a great experience if you actually fire clearblade and hire a mobile development team that has more than two weeks of mobile product experience. 

This app gets one star for being technically functional (and because 0 stars is not an option). Everything else about it is terrible. If you care about native app experiences, home automation, or integration - don’t buy a Rheem water heater or thermostat. 

Rheem - this isn’t hard. Enable matter on your thermostat, break up with clearblade, and roll out a mobile app that’s not an embarrassment to an otherwise proud brand. Or just actually get a full partnership with ecobee on a communicating thermostat. 

Ugh. This app is terrible. I miss my ecobee.

author: EJL Killarny
title: Always has issues
body:
Inevitably, this app will have bugs every few months. Whether its defaulting everyone’s time zone to GMT and rendering our schedules useless, or being unable to connect to new devices, or what’s happening right now which is the app is crashing on opening, it’s always something.

But I think the worst part is how inaccessible support is. All tech or smart home apps have bugs. But with Rheem, it feels like there is never any urgency to solve the problems. Troubleshooting tips are not readily available online and calling support usually creates more issues than it solves.

I experience issues with this app 10x more than I do with any of its competitors.

author: Bloody-Nine
title: Does not work with devices purchased outside of the US
body: I own a Rheem water heater in the US and was confident buying another for my second home in Colombia - same brand, same reliability, or so I thought. The problem is that the app required to control this device is not available in the US App Store. To download it, you need a Colombian Apple ID, which requires signing out of your current account. But when you try to sign out from another country, Apple’s theft-protection kicks in and blocks you. Rheem is essentially selling a smart device with an app that’s inaccessible to international homeowners. A product this connected should work across regions, or at minimum, Rheem should be upfront about this limitation before purchase.

body: This is our second gladiator hot water heater.  Already having an issue with warning of leak detection.  No water anywhere.  Looking for help. Second plumber said the pipe works was bad and put in shark bite fittings    They worked great and no waiting for them   Now the leak detector keeps going off but no water anywhere we can see. Water got in there after removing fittings blew out the water and cleaned it up and dried it out.  No water anywhere we can see.  Used toilet paper to see if there was water anywhere.  Nothing but a beeping alarm and when we turn it off.  It shuts off the water to the house.  So we have to press the reset to get the water flowing again into the house.  Then like 5 minutes later the alarm goes off again.  So we just turned the alarm off so we can have hot water    Any help appreciated

author: Runi Runs It
title: Major issues with this app, ***DEVELOPERS READ!***
body:
After years of using this app with the HP water heater, please fix the following ASAP!
1)  With the latest update we have lost the option to turn the water heater “Off” within the schedule.   This is possibly one of the most important features needed, to turn the WH off at certain time slots, why remove it? FIX ASAP!
2)  “Heat pump only” mode should be just that! Nothing but the heat pump should ever run when in this mode!  As it’s currently configured, if the water temperature is roughly 7-10° or more below the set-point, the resistive electric heaters kick on using major electric electricity. Fix ASAP!
3)  “Heat pump only” mode should obviously be the most energy efficient mode, yet “Energy Savings” mode is constantly pushed as being the most energy efficient.  “Heat pump only” should be the most energy efficient and never use anything other than the heat pump (as outlined above).  “Energy Savings” mode should always use the heat pump UNLESS the water temperature gets say 10° below the set point.  There are pages of debates and testing on forums currently over these confusing modes.  Fix them as I outlined to remove all the confusion and so the user can force the unit to use only the heat pump at all times if desired allowing more energy efficiency!
4)  Add more lines to the schedule.  We need at least two more time slots, preferably more!
5)  Show the actual water temperature within the tank on the app. This data is available, show this VERY useful information!
6)  The app is occasionally glitchy and sometimes has to be closed and reopened multiple times for setting changes to actually take place.
7)  We are currently forced to share personal information on the app.  In this day and age with all the cyber security concerns, nobody wants their personal information out there!  It’s not like Rheem is contacting us when there is a problem, so remove it.
8)  Within the usage graphs, please add the day and or date when a bar data is selected.  It currently only shows energy used when highlighted. It’s frequently difficult to read or match up the time with the highlighted bar.

Please fix all these items ASAP and you will fix the majority of the frequent consumer complaints about this app! TY!

title: Totally unreliable
body:
Update Oct 2025: after speaking with a tech representative, Rheem spent a couple weeks before they resolved my ticket and they said it was resolved and so far it does seem like the scheduling is working as it should so I’m going to improve my rating.
This app worked fine for a month other than once or twice it did not follow the schedule I set and I didn’t have hot water (still unacceptable). It was not due to my Wi-Fi or my power being out (my house is very automated, and I have record of whether those things happen). Then after a month or two it stopped following my schedule totally. Every morning I would notice it never turned on and I would have to turn it on manually. I have to close and reopen the app to get it to communicate with the water heater again. It loses communication very often now and I’ve given up on trying to use the app. I’ve resorted to installing a $150 high amperage Z-Wave switch, and I’m shutting the water heater on and off myself to follow my time of use energy plan, which is what the water heater schedule was supposed to do in the first place. I shouldn’t have to do this for a “smart” water heater. It would be nice if Rheem reimbursed me for that switch. Their tech support said they know about this issue and they added me to a list of people to contact whenever they do resolve it but I’m not keeping my hopes up.

author: Jim_Laurent
title: Gives confusing information about Rheem Water Heater
body:
This is an awful app with a number of problems that I had to call the Rheem Tech support about.  In the Health screen:  The statements about compressor life and element health are fine.  What is the meaning of green, yellow, red bars?  There is some red. Is that bad? Why does one have more red than the other? What exactly are they measuring? Time remaining? Functionality?  If all is normal, shouldn’t they just be green?  The device is brand new, why any red or yellow?    Available hot water 2/3 full doesn’t make sense to the consumer.  Better indicator would be Upper and Lower Elements temperatures as view on the front console using Test mode. I’ve been gone two days with “I’m away” setting.  Set temp is 125. Available hot water is full.  This doesn’t make sense.  Set temp should be whatever the Vacation temp setting is and available hot water should be zero. (Better yet, actual upper and lower element temperature.). If the system is in “Away” or “Vacation” mode, set temp should be something like 80º.

Mode still says “Energy saver” after app restart when it should say Vacation.

The device is lying to me!   The Entire Heat Pump Water Heater acts as a button to allow you to make changes.  It’s not intuitive that it should be clicked.  I suggest a button. “Click to make changes”
Mode Should be “Heating Mode.”
What’s the difference between “Status” and “State” These are two words for the same thing. Please qualify.
I suggest: “Heating Element Status:”  Compressor Running, Electric Elements on, Off
When the element is not running, “Status” disappears. It should still be there but display the “Off” option.  
Power Status On/Off
Also, Compressor Running is improperly truncated.

author: Marc O99
title: False Advertising
body:
I just bought/installed a RHEEM Professional Prestige ProTerra heat pump water heater, in large part due to this feature on their spec sheet: “Built-in Wi-Fi powered by EcoNet®2 and free mobile app gives users control over water heater, ­allowing for customizable temperature, ­vacation
settings, ­energy savings and system monitoring at home or away”. 

I wanted to schedule water heating to avoid peak electricity rates and best use solar power in the future. Scheduling initially didn’t work and now the app stopped working entirely (can’t even login). 

If you’re considering buying a RHEEM water heater and counting on using this capability, DON’T. 

I called Rheem Customer Service a week ago and got no useful response (“we’re aware of it…”). I see online comments going back 3 years about similar issues. Looks like they aren’t serious about meeting their claims and commitments (SW dev/QA). How do I get my money back?

title: Bug for Off/Disable persists once a month.
body:
Extremely frustrated. A while back there was a bug that the heater would occasionally not turn back on when the schedule had a time period set to off/disabled. They mostly fixed this, except that the last day of the month it happens again. Every month. February 28, March 31, April 30, etc. and I can’t seem to get anyone at Rheem to acknowledge or fix since the bug doesn’t occur as often now, despite being very repeatable. 

They just recommend to not use the off/disable feature, but it’s very close to working except this monthly bug resulting in no hot water.

I have time of use metering so this is a needed feature for me. The alternative would be if they allowed you to set a lower temperature than 110 (like, 80F). That would let me leave the water heater in “on” mode all the time, but allow me to delay its use until my lower electricity rates. 

I sure wish someone would either be compelled to fix the once a month issue or add this other feature to set a much lower temperature, which would negate my need to use the off/disable feature.

author: Trishatinabeana
title: Application no longer allows me to clear alerts remotely
body:
I’m not sure what software update got pushed that no longer allows for alert clearance remotely but it’s supremely annoying. I have to physically go reset my water heater every time now. I’ve tried everything - deleting and uninstalling the app, fresh connection, etc. I get a text to my phone number that the device has an A102 sensor alert, but open the app and there is zero notification, nor any option to override the alert if I DO get an app notification. 
Which means I have to get up and go out the water heater and reset it manually EVERY. FREAKING. TIME. This never use to happen and it was frankly the most useful feature on the app. At this point the leak sensor sensitivity to humidity and frequent shut offs is making me want to rip the sensor out entirely. I hated this water heater from the jump because of that, but the apps ability to override was the reason I kept it. Please bring that feature back or give me a useful user guide/documentation that shows me how to force override via the app so I don’t find out at 10pm at night when I’m trying to get ready for bed that I suddenly have no hot water.

author: androidOneEleven
title: No.
body:
We replaced our downstairs HVAC unit, and while I had some minor issues with setup, it works. We replaced our upstairs unit a few months later, and can’t get the app connected / new unit recognized reliably. Rheem noted it would be fixed in the next major update after 6.9.0, but the last version says it improved connectivity and it certainly didn’t for us.

The biggest issue for me is the idea that a company as big/successful as this one will not or cannot get an arguably critically important component of the system working on iOS. 

FWIW our units were replaced due to them being old; one started emitting CO and had to be replaced immediately, the other needed work each year & we didn’t want it to fail in the middle of a heat wave. It also had a splitting heating component that would have failed in the next heating season, which, ironically, was every day this past week.

Apparently there are no issues with setup/connectivity on Android.

Simply put: Connectivity is very important to us, and as it’s part of the system, it’s part of what we paid for; if we had time to research systems and found the ongoing iOS issues, we would have looked elsewhere. 

This seems to be an example of what happens when there are no real-world repercussions for failure.

Update 03-20-25.

**Buyer Beware—Do not purchase a Rheem smart water heater until they address their broken Econet app integration.**

Additionally, old version of app allows for temp change updates without having to be in schedule mode , which is disabled in newest app version. 

Econet tech support is useless. Called Rheem, spoke with “Brenda” for over an hour; she had very limited tech knowledge, and I was able to get system reconnected on my own. 

Solution for RHEEM— examine the functionality of the prior version of your app and update the current app to maintain that same level of functionality for the current iOS version. The latest version of your app is broken clearly, and your developers need to take another look at what they broke in this latest version.

author: Puh22
title: Schedule not respected
body:
1. I want the heat pump OFF during peak ToU period. But the history shows that it’s consuming energy then. Grr. 

2. The Rheem energy’s core page perpetually shows “cannot be calculated”. So it’s just an annoying page to have to get past, that provides no value. 

3. Please explain why energy saver mode is more efficient than heat pump only mode. This is hard to believe. 

4. The graph bars don’t line up to the labels. 

5. The graphs are hard to read because they’re the last 24 hours. Even if you go back to previous days. Just simplify and make it for the day from midnight to midnight. 

6. Too many steps with waiting at each step to get to the usage graphs. 

7. Animated splash screen adds friction and doesn’t contribute to “the best possible user experience”

8. Release notes are often non descriptive. 

9. Most of us have only one Rheem heater. So that front page where you select your heater only serves as another friction point to get past. When there’s only one heater (the 80% case) just skip this page. 

10. “Available hot water” metric is too dumbed down. It depends on the set point temperature too so as the schedule changes the “fullness” can change. C’mon give us something more specific and usable.

11. There’s no indication that the information you’re looking at is outdated, because the app has not yet synched to the state of the heater. You just need to say “as of 3 hours ago.” And then update that when you get new data. 

I think a lot of these issues would be discovered if the team just went out and visited a handful of real users using the app for five minutes.

author: Noah Coccaro
body: 1. The app does not update the status of the hot water heater unless you force close it by swiping away, and reopening it. Otherwise it will show the same empty tank for hours. 2. The graph for energy usage for the day is in increments of 1/2 hour. But the data is only in increments of 1 hour. So each hour shows the usage, and each half hour shows 0, which makes it look like the heater cycles every half hour, which it does not. 3. If in set up, your phone connects to 5Ghz WiFi, it will fail. You must force your phone to connect to the router in 2.4GHz band. I did this by moving far enough away, and behind a metal shed to block the weaker 5ghz band and connect with 2.4ghz band. 4. Sometimes when updating the schedule, the updates don't appear to be saved, and get reverted. I don't know if that's because the app doesn't update unless you force close, or if it is because you need to press "Save" multiple times. 5. Other than the above, the app seems to work to adjust schedules, and report current status, though it does not report current temperature of the hot water, just what it is set to go up to. So if your schedule has it go from 120 to 150, you won't know how close to 150 you are at. (you'd only do this if you had a thermostatic mixing valve to blend cold water with the 150 degree water)

author: A Google user
body: Being able to get alerts and control my water heater(s) from anywhere in the world is great, but this app could be much better. Be aware that the app functions differently for different models. I have a Gladiator and a Platinum Hybrid (at different locations). It's like different companies chose the features for each model. 1) The app does not display the current water temperature! For the Gladiator, an "Available Hot Water" meter is displayed giving you some idea of whether water is up to the set temperature. For the Hybrid, nothing is displayed to indicate whether the water is up to the set temperature. You have to go to the physical water heater and look at the display on the unit. This severely limits functionality of the app for the top of line Hybrid water heaters. The app should display the upper and lower temperatures and it would be nice to view all of the sensor data visible on the unit's display. 2) Scheduling is limited to 4 time periods per day. It's not enough. For a high demand period, I want to ramp up to temperature in efficient mode before the high demand starts, then keep it in high demand mode, then return to efficient mode at a lower temperature. This requires 3 time periods. With only 4 time periods to program, you cannot properly setup more than one demand period per day. It would be more effective to have at least 6 time periods per day. 3) The Gladiator version provides an "Element Health" indicator that is not present for the Hybrid version. Why not? Both have electric elements. Update 2/23/20: Power was shut off to the w/h for a little while today. It seemed to lose the latest schedule settings but retained *SOME* of the schedule?!? It lost the 4AM setting, but kept the 7AM and 9AM settings. This makes no sense. Trying to set the schedule again and it will not save! Changed 3 time periods for Monday, pressed Save. Message on screen says "Schedule Saved". Go back and view the schedule - the changes are were not saved. Tried turning off "Follow Schedule". It will not turn off. Tried several times. Found that my phone was connected to my 5Ghz wifi and w/h is on 2.5Ghz. Switching my phone to 2.5Ghz to match the w/h got the schedule functions working. So why was showing a different schedule when I was connected on a different wifi??

author: A Google user
body: This is a pretty poorly designed app. The developers must have gone to some lengths to make the interface different and more confusing than what appears on the screen of the thermostat itself. Some bits are simply not functional at all (try setting "Night" temperatures when scheduling, for example). And the Home/Away setting button in the middle of the screen which proclaims the exact opposite of your current status (its label is "I'm Home" when in fact I am away, and vice versa) is ridiculously counterintuitive...why not label this "Set Home" when away and "Set Away" when home? And in spite of what previous reviewer Bill Lin says, this does not provide any "energy charts or graphs"...I think he is getting this confused with Ecobee which is a better thermostat/app combination in almost every way. For basic remote access to turning the temp up and down and this app is sufficient. I'd swap this thermostat and app out with Ecobee in a heartbeat if it were not for Rheem's proprietary communications interface with their hvac systems.

body: So I read that Rheem says they've redesigned the whole platform... Well, let me tell you, they did it wrong!  For those who are still holding onto hope and struggling to get this set-up, I'll describe what the app is trying to do. so that you can make adjustments accordingly.  1. The app makes you create an account.  So you must have Internet access.  2, Then it wants you to DISCONNECT from the Internet, and connect the the hotspot that the module is creating (called ECONETxxxxx)  3. Once connected to the module directly, it wants you to enter, or rather select your network, and enter your network password.  However, it falls short on two fronts:   3a. The module ONLY operates on the older 2.4GHz spectrum, so if your home network is running 802.11a (5GHz), then you won't see it.   3b  Also, if you have a hidden SSID, the app/module does not give you an option to enter the network manually. BOTH OF THESE REDESIGNED ITEMS ARE FAILS!  4. Once you've entered your network's credentials, the app wants you to reconnect to the same network you've just entered into the module.  It checks to see that it's there, and then you're up and running.  Poorly redesigned!

body: This was an expensive water heater and then more for the WIFI module.  I could not successfully register the device even though I'm a software engineer with an entire house of working wifi and z-wave products. And I tried to register with iPhone app, Android app and web browser.   It would go through the whole process connecting to both the econet wifi from the device as well as my home network. Then it would display the correct MAC address of the device and a finish button. Hit the finish and it says it can't find the same MAC adddress device it just displayed!  At the last stage of registration, the device WIFI stops working. The network no longer shows up on available WIFI list, but the WIFI icon is on as though it were really working. Rheem could not solve the problem. Didn't even try. We'll call you back in a few days because we THINK the server may not be functioning. What?  I can return this WIFI unit. But I'm stuck with a very expensive water heater that I only bought for the WIFI capability. First water heater install had a leaking tank. Had to return heater and get another install.
